title.narrative: IUCN Naturbaserade lösningar för resilienta samhällen
IUCN Nature-based Solutions for Resilient Communities in the Western Balkans

description.narrative:
Overall objective of the project: Increased ecosystem and community resilience to climate change and environmental degradation in the Western Balkans Objective 1: Enhance knowledge and awareness of nature-based disaster risk reduction solutions among decision makers, natural resource managers and local communities Objective 2: Enhance integration of Nature-based Solutions and climate-smart planning into adaptation and disaster risk reduction policy Objective 3: Increase implementation of nature-based disaster risk reduction solutions
The contribution is expected to demonstrate how nature based solutions can reduce vulnerability to natural disasters and at the same time create livelihood opportunities for people depending on ecosystem services. The work on capacity building will build awareness about nature based solutions among general public and decision makers. The implementation of concrete nature based solutions in Serbia and Albania will serve as a demonstration site for other countries in the Region.

Den regionala insatsen ADAPT: Nature-based Solutions for Resilient Societies in the Western Balkans kommer att genomföras i Albanien, Kosovo, Bosnien och Hercegovina, Nord Makedonien, Montenegro och Serbien. Projektet syftar till att visa hur naturbaserade lösningar kan komplettera tekniska lösningar i arbetet med klimatanpassning och katastrofriskreducering. Projektet är ett pilotprojekt för att implementera naturbaserade lösningar i Albanien och Serbien, sprida kunskap om naturbaserade lösningar bland allmänhet och beslutsfattare i regionen.
Projektet fokuserar på områden utsatta för effekter av klimatförändringar som tex översvämningar och kommer därmed att bidra till arbetet med katastrofriskreducering, klimatanpassning, biologisk mångfald och miljöhänsyn. Indirekt kommer projektet genom ett väl integrerat jämställdhetsperspektiv och rättighetsperspektiv bidra till att visa hur miljöhänsyn kan skapa förutsättningar för ökad jämställdhet och demokratisering. Avsikten är också att denna insats utgör en start till ett större projekt att ansöka från gröna klimatfonden.

The ADAPT: Nature-based Solutions for Resilient Societies in the Western Balkan project aims to demonstrate how nature based solutions can complement engineering solutions in disaster risk reduction. The project will identify solutions on how nature can improve; water security; food security; solutions for disaster risk reduction; and solutions for climate adaptation in Western Balkan with pilots in Albania and Serbia and assessments in BiH, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Kosovo.
The project focuses on areas exposed to effects of climate change such as floods and will thus contribute to the work on disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, biodiversity and environmental considerations. Indirectly, through a well-integrated gender equality and rights perspective, the project will help to show how environmental considerations can create conditions for increased gender equality and democratisation. It is also intended that this effort is a start to a larger project to apply from the Green Climate Fund.

title.narrative: Grant agreement between Sida and IUCN - Western Balkans
Beslut om insats, IUCN reg västra Balkan

description.narrative:
Main results reported by IUCN included:
Component 1: Knowledge, awareness and capacity building
- Publication of the two last scoping studies, on Montenegro and Kosovo, designed to deepen regional insights into NbS.
- Publication of Compendium on best NbS practices, presenting good examples of NbS interventions carried out in the region. This publication, coupled with active collaboration with the Panorama Solutions platform to share information on pilot projects in Albania and Serbia, significantly advanced on-the-ground NbS implementation according to IUCN.
- A study tour to Bonn, Germany, further enhanced stakeholder capacity, involving 18 participants from various Balkan institutions who engaged with international bodies and German government agencies, enriching the regional dialogue on NbS.
Component 2: Policy advocacy and mainstreaming
- Production of policy briefs on the economics, finance, and governance of NbS, following the coordination of a regional Comparative Policy Analysis. These briefs, now available in multiple languages, play a critical role in shaping the legal and policy frameworks necessary for the integration of NbS into regional strategies.
- Active participation in global, regional, and local events, together with local partners. These efforts not only improved project visibility but also facilitated significant networking opportunities with relevant stakeholders.
Component 3: NbS implementation and Scale-up
- Completion of essential preparatory work in North Macedonia, finalizing the tender dossier roadmap for an upcoming NbS pilot project.
- Advance in scaling up NbS in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Kosovo, where prefeasibility studies were initiated to identify suitable project sites. The year concluded with intensive consultations and planning sessions to lay the groundwork for future implementations.
- In Serbia and Albania, despite difficulties in procuring services which postponed some field implementations, significant progress was made in project design and planning in final preparation for field work in both sites.
Impact of activities
The increase in political buy-in on national and municipal level and general awareness of NbS are difficult to measure. The overall feedback from other partners in the region has been positive, and the momentum for incorporating NbS in DRR, urban and climate adaptation planning is definitely rising by each day as the effects of climate change are becoming more and more severe. Climate adaptation, biodiversity conservation and restoration, and climate risk management are areas where inaction can be immediately katastrofic but the results from action are gradual and seeing the impacts of applying best practices takes time. Therefore must this project be seen as a start of a longer process in a systemic change, and a small demonstration on the value of NbS. A lot depends on the initial success and interest raised by the pilot FLR initiatives in Serbia and Albania. Overall, these practical examples are crucial to show-case in order to improve the low understanding of NbS in the Western Balkans.
Community engagement and civil society participation could apparently be improved, even though IUCN is widely networked and has a thorough picture of the field and the relevant actors. IUCN's role and mandate (as one of the regional coordinators of the Action Plan for the Green Agenda), with close ties to government entities and the RCC, might however contribute to scepticism from grassroot civil society.
Sida made no follow-up visit during the reporting period, which is why it is difficult to know exactly how the relationship with local civil society has developed since last reporting period.
The implementation of pilot NbS projects in Albania and Serbia has continued to face obstacles, such as finding a professional contractor to carry out the field work, difficulties in finding seeds and seedlings of the right species, timing of the field works that are dependent on season and weather conditions, managing other land usages in a sustainable way, etc. IUCN has managed to clarify all of the delays to Sida in an open manner, which Sida continues to appreciate. The challenges with pilot projects should be seen as important lessons learned for future initiatives.
Due to the practical challenges the project was granted one last no-cost extension until the end of 2024, in order to finish the pilot activities in the field. Most other activities have been finalised with high quality during the reporting period.
Additional challenges that have contributed to delays but can only be accepted include changes in key staff (Regional Director, Program manager), recruitment challenges, and both project officers having to take longer sick-leaves due to accident and illness.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
